utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Okay so, trial length for the launch, I've been thinking about this all weekend, and honestly I also finally watched that documentary about, never mind. I think we do a fourteen day free trial, no credit card needed.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: No card at all?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: No card. The thing about cards is, nobody wants to type one in for a product they haven't tried. And that's what, like, kills signups. So if we drop that, more teams get in, they actually see it work, and I'd bet conversion to paid goes up.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: I think maybe that's what, um, Slack and those companies did? Early on?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Right, they didn't ask for a card.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Not all of them.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Most.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Devil's advocate: what stops someone from signing up forty times?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Email verification. I mean, that's coming.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: I think it's next month? Maybe.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: It's next month.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: So for a month there's no check.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: It's a launch, you accept some noise.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I'm just flagging.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: I hear it. Let's go with the fourteen day free trial, no card, for launch.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Yes!

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: I'll update the, um, signup page copy.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Good. What else?

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Oh, the logo, the new one, did anyone see it? I think the blue is too, like, corporate.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: It's fine.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: I like the blue.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: I'm outvoted. Okay. Moving on.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Marco, analytics dashboard, ready by the launch?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Yes. Mostly.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Mostly?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Signup funnel is ready. Retention isn't.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Funnel's the one I need.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Then yes.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Great. We meet again in three weeks. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Right, is that everyone? It's two minutes past and I've got the fire people at half ten.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Dmitri's just getting a coffee, he said to start without- oh, there he is.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'm here, I'm here. The machine on three is leaking again, by the way.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: That's ticket 4417, open since the sixth. Which reminds me, the lift.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Oh, the lift. I was in it on Tuesday, the panel was doing that flickering thing, and the chap from-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: That's lift two, it's always lift two.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Lift two, yes. Their service visit moved to the twenty-second, and they've quoted 1,480 pounds for a door sensor.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Shouldn't that sit under the maintenance contract, though? Odd that we'd pay on top.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Contract covers call-outs, not parts.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: And who says a sensor's a part? I mean, they do, obviously, they're the ones billing it.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Clause nine lists door sensors under parts. I checked in November.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Ah. Well, there goes my argument.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thanks, Fatima. So that goes through as normal, I'll raise it today.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Can they do it on a day that isn't the twenty-second, though? Because that's the Friday the, um, the furniture people are bringing the-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: That's the twenty-fourth.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Is it? Right, sorry, the twenty-fourth. Fine, ignore me.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Car park next. We've got 38 permits and 44 requests, and I've had three emails this week already.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: It's the sales lot, they've all-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: It's not only sales, Dmitri, there's four from legal as well.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: You know the bike cage is half empty, I counted, there's eleven in there, and I mean in January who's cycling in, but even so-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Do we actually have to solve that today? Permits renew in April.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: No, April's fine. I just want the list cleaned up, there's still two leavers on it.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: I can do that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay, fourth floor. Refit starts in, what, nine weeks, and we've still got nothing written down for the noise.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: It's dreadful up there now, even with it half empty. You can hear the- you can hear someone unwrapping a sandwich from the far end.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Consultant's report came back at a 0.85 absorption target. That's the number we have to hit, and I need something to take to finance.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yeah, so I've been talking to Tessaline-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Who?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Tessaline, they do a recycled PET felt wall panel, and honestly I'd run it right across the floor, the whole 310 square metres.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: The whole floor? Not just the bits round the meeting rooms?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Whole floor. Otherwise you're just-

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Is that the grey stuff they've got at the Leeds office? Because I went up there for the, what was it, the landlord day, and it looked-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Different supplier, I think. Look, it does the job, right, it reaches the 0.85 target at 62 pounds a square metre, which is about 20 percent under that timber slat quote, and it counts toward the landlord's recycled-content clause.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: 62 times 310, that's 19,220.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Before fixing, yes-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And the slat quote was 77.50 a metre, so 24,025. Yeah, that's your 20 percent.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Fine, but that's their number, isn't it? Who measured the 0.85, them?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: There's a test certificate, I've got it in my-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: A test certificate from them or from a lab?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: From a lab, Kwame. It's on the datasheet.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: I'm only asking. Everything's 0.85 in a brochure.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Felt though. Does felt not go a bit, you know, sad after a few years? My sister had felt tiles in her studio and-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Not the same thing.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: No, no, I know, I'm just saying they went a bit bobbly.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: And it's a wall panel, so somebody's going to lean a chair on it. Someone will stick a poster on it.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fatima, you've read the lease more recently than any of us. Does it actually count?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Yes. The clause wants thirty percent recycled content by value across the fit-out. Felt would help with that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thirty percent by value, right.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Help, or get us there?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Help. It's one line of the fit-out.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Which is more than the timber was going to do-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Sure, I'm not arguing, I'm just saying don't let's oversell it to finance.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Do they come in colours? Because if we're looking at that wall for ten years, I'd quite like it not to be-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: There's a colour card, loads of them.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Colours can wait. Lead time, Dmitri?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Five weeks from order, they said on the phone. That's inside the nine.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Said on the phone.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'll get it in writing, obviously-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Please do. Anything else, Kwame, or are you just enjoying yourself?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Bit of both. No, the price is the price, I can't really knock that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fatima?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: No, it's fine by me.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay. The fourth floor gets the Tessaline felt panels, I'll put that in the note to finance today.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Great, I'll send you the datasheet and the-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And the lead time in writing.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: And the lead time, yes.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Oh, while I think of it, has anyone told the third floor about the drilling? Not this, I mean the riser work next week.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: That's Monday and Tuesday. Notice went out yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: I didn't get it.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: You never read them.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: That's fair, actually.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fire warden rota. We're two short on the second floor since Priya left and Tom went on paternity leave.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Can we not just ask-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I've asked. Nobody's replied. I need 14 wardens across the building for the March drill and I've got 12.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Do we really need 14, or is that just what it's always been?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: One per 25 people, per floor, it's in the fire risk assessment.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Worth a shot.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: I did it for a couple of years at my old place, you get the little hi-vis and everyone completely ignores you, there was this one time-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Are you volunteering?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: I'm not on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: There's a new starter in payroll on two. Ana. She might say yes.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Good thought, I'll drop her a line. The training's the thirtieth, half a day.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Is the thirtieth the same day as the cleaning contract review?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: That's the thirty-first.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Right, okay, because I've got the-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: You've got the dentist, you told us twice.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I've got the dentist.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Last one, the Christmas party invoice. The venue's billed us 2,310 and we agreed 2,130.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Someone's swapped the digits, surely.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Probably. Kwame, you booked it, can you chase them?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: I can, though did we not add the extra hour on the night? I'd want to check before I start shouting.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Check first, then. No shouting either way.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: No promises.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fatima, you've got the permit list. Dmitri, the Tessaline paperwork. I've got the lift, and I'm late for the fire people.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Does anyone want this last biscuit, or-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: So, we've been live three weeks. Marco, numbers.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Nineteen hundred trial signups. Three point one percent converted to paid. And about forty percent of the signups used throwaway or fake emails.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Three percent isn't bad for three weeks. I mean, trials need time, they're fourteen days, so some haven't even-

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: I excluded those.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: Forty percent, that's, I think, a lot?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: It's a lot. And I think this is exactly what I was worried about. A no-card trial attracts people who never meant to pay, and some who are just abusing it. Those fake signups cost us about eleven hundred dollars a month in compute, and they wreck the funnel numbers, so we can't even tell what real conversion is. We need a card up front.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Eleven hundred a month is nothing next to what we'd lose if-

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: It's nothing now. It's launch.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: Could, um, email verification fix some of it?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Next month. Doesn't fix people with real throwaway addresses.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Wait, are those fake or just, like, privacy people?

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Mostly obvious junk. Mailinator, stuff like that.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Sofia, what would you do?

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Seven-day trial, card required. Seven days is enough for a real team to try it, and the card filters out the people who aren't serious.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Seven days is short. People have a week with meetings, they don't touch anything till day five.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Real teams will. Serious ones, I mean.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: I think maybe seven could work, if onboarding is quick? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Onboarding's ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to decide. We switch to a seven day trial, credit card required up front.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Hm. Okay. I disagree but okay.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Noted.

utterances.speaker: Nadia
utterances.text: I'll change the copy again.

utterances.speaker: Omar
utterances.text: Wasn't that the thing we literally changed last, never mind.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Marco, track it. Signups, conversion, both.

utterances.speaker: Marco
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Also the email verification date, is it fixed?

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Next month, the fifteenth.

utterances.speaker: Sofia
utterances.text: Good.

utterances.speaker: Diego
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay, it's four minutes past, so let's go. Lift first, because that one's quick.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Is it still the twenty-second? Because I told the-

utterances.text: Still the twenty-second. Parts order's raised, 1,480 plus VAT.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: And the coffee machine on three, is that-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Ticket 4417, closed Wednesday. New seal, no charge.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: It's still dripping.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Then reopen it, Dmitri, I can't fix it from here.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Did anyone actually look at it, or did they just close the ticket?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: They looked at it, they stood there, they had a coffee-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Reopen it. Fatima, the permit list?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Done. Two leavers off, so 36 names on 38 permits.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: 36 against 44 requests, then. Thanks. Parked till April anyway.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Ana said yes, by the way, to the warden thing, I saw her at the lifts, she's quite keen actually, she asked if she gets the-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: She emailed me. That's 13 of 14, so I'm still one short for the March drill.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: What about-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I've asked him. Kwame, the Christmas invoice?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Yeah, the extra hour. We did add it, on the night, 180 quid, so 2,310 is right and I was all set to shout for nothing.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Good thing you checked. I'll pay it. Who signed for the hour?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Me, apparently. It's my signature, sadly.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: That was a good hour, though.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Right, fourth floor. Finance came back Tuesday, they're fine with the 19,220 plus fixing. Dmitri, paperwork?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Got it, got the lead time in writing, finally. They've got enough on the shelf to hit the installers' slot, as long as the order's with them by the twenty-fourth.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: So the third of February holds.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: The third holds, I've got the fitters booked in, and the order form's in your inbox, it just wants your name on it and-

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Sorry. Before that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Go on, Fatima.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: The insurer's surveyor was in on Wednesday, for the renewal walk-round. I took him up to four and mentioned the panels.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: What's he got to do with-

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: He says escape-corridor linings have to reach Euroclass B-s1,d0, and I checked Dmitri's datasheet, and the Tessaline test certificate only shows C-s2,d0.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Hang on, which certificate, the one I sent round?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: The one you sent Ravi on the tenth. Page three.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: B-s1,d0 against C-s2,d0. Say that again, the first one's the requirement?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: B is what he wants. C is what they've got.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: But that's for corridors, right, that's not a whole floor thing, it's not like the open-plan-

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: He only talked about the escape corridors.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Oh, that's the same chap, is it, big fellow, the fleece with the logo? Because when I had my loft done the insurance sent one of these people, not him, obviously, but the same sort, and he spent forty minutes on the hatch, an actual loft hatch, and then wanted a letter from the man who fitted it-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Henrik.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: and that man had moved to Portugal, is the thing, so we ended up ringing his brother, who does kitchens in Stockport, and he-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Does this end with a fire certificate?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: It ends with me paying sixty pounds for a new hatch, so, sort of, yes.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thank you, Henrik. Dmitri, how does a panel get a C?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I don't know, it's felt, it's a fire class, it was on the sheet the whole time and nobody-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Nobody read that bit, no. Everyone was looking at the 0.85.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: You weren't exactly reading it either, you were asking who the lab was.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: True. I'm reading it now, though. Fatima, did he put this in writing?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Not yet. He said it'll be in his report.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: When's that due?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: He said about two weeks.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: So that's the end of the month. We can't sit on it till then, the order has to go by the twenty-fourth or we lose the slot-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Yes, and that's rather my point, Dmitri. If Ravi puts his name on that form as it stands and we've got a known C on an escape route, that could void the building cover, and the fitters walk in on the third of February.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Could. Could void. He's a surveyor, he's not the-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: He's the insurer's surveyor, it's the insurer's policy. Who else's opinion would you like?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I'm saying he said a thing in a corridor-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: And now we know he said it, that's what's changed. Claim on a fire with that in an email chain, how do you think that goes?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Is it the whole building, though? The cover? Not just four?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: It's one policy, as far as I know. Ravi?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: One policy, the renewal's 1 April. I'd have to check the wording. I don't want to guess at that.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Okay, but how many metres are we talking? Out of the 310, how much of it is even corridor?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I don't have that. Does anyone have that?

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: The old plan had the corridor sort of wrapping round the core, but the new layout moves the-

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: It doesn't move it-

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: It moves the kitchen, I'm sure it moves the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I need a number, not the kitchen. Dmitri, can you measure it off the refit drawings?

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Yeah, I can do that today. I'd also like to ask Tessaline what the C actually means, whether it's the test or whether-

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: You'd like to ask the people selling it.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Who would you ask, Kwame?

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: I'm only saying, you know, ask, but don't bring me another phone call.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: In writing, same as the lead time. Fatima, can you get hold of the surveyor before his report's out? Even an email, just with the exact wording.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: I've got his card. I'll try him today.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thanks. And I'll ask legal, or whoever reads the policy, what it actually says about linings. That's three things and today's the seventeenth.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: So where does that leave the order? Because the twenty-fourth is Friday, it's a week, and Tessaline will want to know-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Nothing changes on paper yet. It's still the Tessaline felt, finance has it, I just want to see those three answers before we talk about it again.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: And the form?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: It's in my inbox, Kwame, I know where it is. We'll come back to it.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Monday's meeting?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'm off Monday. Offline, then, I'll find a slot next week.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: I've got the cleaning contract on the thirty-first, is that still-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Thirty-first, yes, ten o'clock. I've got their renewal at 41,600 a year, up 6 percent, so bring the complaints log.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Six? On what basis?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Wage uplift, they say. That's for the thirty-first, not now.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Are we still doing the Thursday deep clean on two, because the carpet by the printers-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Log it, Henrik. Same as the machine.

utterances.speaker: Dmitri
utterances.text: Speaking of which, I'm going to go and reopen 4417.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Do. Fatima, you'll send me whatever you get from him?

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: Kwame
utterances.text: Nice catch, by the way. Page three.

utterances.speaker: Fatima
utterances.text: It was only because he asked.

utterances.speaker: Henrik
utterances.text: Did he ask about the loft hatch on five? Because that one doesn't close properly either.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: We're done, thanks everyone.

utterances.text: It's priced, yeah, eleven thousand a year. But hold on, that's the part-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Eleven thousand is not nothing.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It's not, but let me finish. We're already licensed for the platform, so there's no new vendor, no new contract, nothing to onboard.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Mm. Um, go on.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: And configuring it is about two weeks, they said. Two weeks of setup. There's no data migration, because the vendors and the GL codes are already sitting in there.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Two weeks, that sounds, I mean, that sounds optimistic. When we did the expense thing it was, what, six?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That was a different thing, that moved data from three places. This doesn't move anything.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay but what do we actually get out of it? Like, in numbers.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Right, so I pulled the timestamps from last quarter. Median time from invoice received to approved is nine days right now. With routing in the module it should land around three.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Nine days? Median? Not the average?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Median. The average is worse, there's a long tail of stuff stuck over a month.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Is that, um, nine days including the ones that go to the regional offices?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Yes, all of it.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay. That's, yeah. That's a lot.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It's a lot. I think maybe, um, it also affects the early-pay discounts, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It does, we've been missing a couple of those.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Speaking of discounts, did you see what happened with the freight vendor? They sent a statement with, like, the same invoice listed twice and-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Is that this topic?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: No, no. Not really. It's just funny. They had it twice and one had a different PO number.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Pavel, can you, um, maybe send that to Umar? He handles the freight stuff.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Yeah, I'll forward it today.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Okay. Back to- can I push on the price a bit?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Go ahead, that's fair.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Eleven thousand a year, every year. If we get a better tool in six months we're, we're stuck paying that?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It's annual. We could stop renewing. And what's the alternative, nothing? Because right now the cost is people chasing approvals by hand.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'm not saying nothing. I'm saying, did anyone look-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, Ravi, I think nobody has brought another one to me. Has someone?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: No. Not yet. I just don't love picking the first thing we see.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: It's also the one with the least risk, though. Honestly I'd argue it's the boring choice and that's why it works.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Can I ask about permissions?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Please, yes.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Um, so the, the approval limits. Who sets those? Because right now it's kind of, it lives in Stefan's head.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: They'd be set up in the config. Tiers by amount, and by cost center. We'd need to write them down first, which we should do anyway.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay. That's good. That, that would help me.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Oh, that reminds me, the audit people wanted the thresholds written down too. Last year they asked and we sort of, we showed them an email from, from like twenty-nineteen.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Not great.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Not great, no.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So that, that's another reason, I think. Um.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Right. It gives us a paper trail without extra work.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fine, but two weeks of whose time? Because month-end is coming.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Mostly mine and the ERP admin's. Maybe a few hours from Pavel for the vendor master cleanup.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: A few hours I can do. If it's, you know, not the week of the close.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yeah, okay. Um. Does anyone, does anybody have a real objection? Like something that would stop us?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Not a stop. I'd want the renewal date in writing, so we know when we can walk.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I'll ask for it. I'll put it in the order form request.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Then I'm okay.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I'm okay with it too. I mean, yes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Good. Pavel, could you get the configuration work on the calendar, with the ERP admin, for maybe the first week after the close? Um, sorry, I mean, something like that.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Sure. I'll check what Sanne's free, uh, I mean the admin's free, and send invites tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Send me the draft so I can block the days.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Will do.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thank you. Um, and I'll tell Emeka we have a plan, he'll be glad.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Tell him the nine days number. He likes numbers.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I will. Okay, other things. Did anybody hear about the team lunch?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Is that the Thursday one? Because I have the thing with, uh, the- no, sorry, I have a thing Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Maybe Friday then. Ivan, does Friday work?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Friday's fine.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Friday's good for me, I'm in anyway.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I can do Friday if it's before one. I've got a call.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, I think maybe noon. I'll ask the place if they have a table for five.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Tomasz might want to come too, he was asking.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Then six. Okay, I'll, um, I'll check. Right, I think that's it. I have to jump to another call.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Yep, go.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay, third meeting, let's go through where we are. Event platform, Noor?

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: I looked at three. The one I like is four dollars an attendee and handles registration and reminders automatically.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: For how many attendees?

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: We're aiming for eight hundred registrants, so about thirty-two hundred.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I think, maybe, that's fine? I remember another vendor wanted seven dollars.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Four is fine.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Sign up for it. Lakshmi, the reception, we need a guest list.

utterances.speaker: Lakshmi
utterances.text: I have, um, forty-two names. Top accounts by revenue, plus a few renewals at risk.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Forty-two for a room that fits forty. That'll be fine, not everyone comes.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: They always come for the free food.

utterances.speaker: Lakshmi
utterances.text: I think about thirty will come.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Catering, maybe a local caterer, small plates.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Budget?

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Around three thousand for thirty.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Okay. Elif, rep sign-ups.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Forty-one signed up. Ahead of target for the smaller event, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Great. Ivan, newsletter.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Yes. I wrote the piece about the showcase. Maybe it's a little long? I can cut it.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Send it to me. And put the start date in.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I think the date is the twenty-first? Starting?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: The twenty-second. I wrote it down.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Right, the twenty-second. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: We need product demo clips for the showcase.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: I can record them in the office on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: I'll help, I'll bring a light.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Also, quick, the office heating. Facilities says it's fixed.

utterances.speaker: Lakshmi
utterances.text: It was freezing yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: They say fixed. We'll see.

utterances.speaker: Noor
utterances.text: Big picture, are we all set for the reception layout?

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Next week. Lakshmi, sketch it.

utterances.speaker: Lakshmi
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: Greta
utterances.text: Anything else? No. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, um, I think we're all here. How was everyone's week, did the lunch place work out?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: The lunch was great. Did you see the dessert they brought out? The one with the burnt sugar on top, my grandmother used to make something like that, she'd-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: It was fine. Is Tomasz joining today?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No, he's on audit prep with Stefan this morning.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Which reminds me, is the March close calendar final?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think maybe it is. Stefan said he'd send the final one Monday.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I have his draft. Cutoff is the fourth, I believe.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: The fourth, okay. Last time I had the wrong date and it still bugs me.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Quick thing before I forget. Who's covering the bank rec Friday?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: I can. I'm in all day.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Great, thanks.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Oh, speaking of the bank, did anyone see the new login page? They moved the whole token thing to a different button and I spent ten minutes-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Pavel, um, maybe we can come back to that.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Right, sorry. Later.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: So, I had a call yesterday that I should tell you about. It's about the invoice approval thing.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: The ERP module?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes. I phoned the account rep to ask about the order form. The renewal date, mostly.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Did he send it?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: He did, that's fine. But then he mentioned something I really didn't expect, and he said it like it was old news.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Uh oh.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: The module we picked, the bundled one, they stop supporting it at the end of this year. After December there are no security patches for it, none.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Wait, none? For something that would be handling payment approvals?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: That's, yeah. That's not good.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: No. And I don't, um, I don't think we can sign for it knowing that. So I think maybe we need to open the question again and look at what else is out there.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fair. Nobody can argue with that.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay, I'll be the annoying one. Is it really a problem? A year of use is a year of use. We could just replace it later.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, maybe. But we'd be doing the setup twice. Two weeks of config, then again.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: True. I'm only asking.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And the auditors. They'd ask about unpatched stuff straight away.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: They would. Okay, fine, I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: So what are we looking at? The other one, the, the one with the capture feature?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes, that one. The standalone one. I think it was twenty-six thousand a year, from the quote.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Twenty-six. Versus eleven. That's, that's more than double.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Not even a little bit double. It's a lot more than double. Sorry, I mean, it's a lot.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It is. Um, I'm not saying that's nothing.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Is it a new vendor then? New contract and all that?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes. Legal would need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: How long does legal take on a thing like that?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I think maybe two or three weeks, if nothing weird is in it. I can ask Marisol.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Marisol's good with these. She was fast on the freight one.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Okay, so, can I say something about why that one makes sense? Because I looked at it again last night.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Please, yes.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: So the thing is, it's got its own support team. If something breaks, it's their problem, not some ticket with the ERP people that sits for a month.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Mm.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And it pulls in our vendor list and account codes straight from the ERP, so no retyping that stuff, no master cleanup.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: That's a big one, honestly.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: And the real thing, the invoices. We get something like fourteen hundred a month, right? Roughly seventy percent of those are PDFs sitting in an email.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: That sounds about right. Most of mine are.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: The capture reads those. So nobody is keying them in. When I did the math on the typing time it comes to about sixty hours a month. Maybe a bit over.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Sixty hours a month. That's like, more than a person's week.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: A week and a half, probably.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Does it read badly scanned ones? Because we get some of those from the regional offices.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Those would still need someone, I'd think. It's the clean PDFs that work. That's the seventy.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay. That's still most of it.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Who checks the reads? Like, when it gets an amount wrong?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: There's a review screen, I think. Somebody confirms before it goes to approval.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay. Good, I just wondered.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And the approval limits would work the same?

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I believe so, tiers by amount. I'd want to see it again to be sure.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, we can ask for a second demo. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I want to see that before we sign anything. The scanned ones especially.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes, that's reasonable.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Hey, Pavel, do you remember who ran the first demo? Last time you said it was Marisol and then it was Sanne.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: It was Sanne. Okay, I admit it was Sanne.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Told you.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: You did. In my head she's always in the green jacket, though.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, let's, um. Let me think about the whole thing for a second.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Take your time.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: The old one has no patches after December. The other one costs more but saves a lot of typing, and it has someone to call. So, the standalone accounts payable automation tool is what we're adopting. I'll tell Emeka today, and I'll ask Marisol to start on the contract.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Okay. I'll send you the questions I have for the second demo.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: And the budget? Eleven was already approved, the other fifteen is-

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I'll take that to Emeka as well. He'll want it in writing.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Yeah, he will.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Do we tell the ERP rep anything?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, not yet. I think maybe after the contract. I don't want to burn the renewal date before we know.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Makes sense.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Pavel, can you pull the invoice counts by month for Emeka? He'll ask.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Sure. I can have it by Wednesday. Probably Tuesday, if the report doesn't hang again.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Wednesday's fine.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Wait, I do have one more thing about that report, there's a filter that sorts by the posting date and not the received date, which-

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: We've been through this.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Fine. I'll just fix it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay. Other things. Did the intern thing get sorted, the desk?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: They put her near the window, I think. By Sanne.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Does she have a login yet?

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Not yet. I asked Tomasz, he said Thursday.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Thursday, okay.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Um, anyone else have anything?

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: The expense policy. Someone said the meal limit changed.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Oh. I think maybe it went up, but I haven't seen the memo.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: I'll look for it.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: I heard fifty-five. Per day. Or was that per trip?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: I'd wait for the memo.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes. Let's wait for that. Okay, I need to go, I have another call at eleven.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Thanks, everyone.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Morning. Let's pick the flooring for the Level 4 fit-out today, plus the furniture delivery schedule.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I, um, I've been looking at it. I think we go with luxury vinyl plank, from Norvik Supply.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Why not carpet tile? Everyone's doing carpet tile.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Vinyl plank's about twenty percent cheaper than the carpet tile, it's quick to replace when a section gets damaged, and Norvik can deliver in three weeks.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Norvik delivered the thing for the Level 2 floor on time, which I was surprised by, because their previous driver, you remember, he got lost twice, anyway-

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Sven.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Right. Yes. Good supplier.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is the twenty percent against the quote we have or, like, list?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Against the quote, I think. I can send it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Playing devil's advocate, three weeks is only three weeks if nothing slips.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: They've got stock.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Big picture, finance wants the floor signed off before the lease incentive ends. So three weeks matters more than anything. Mateo, you're sure about the stock?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: They confirmed Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Fine by me. Mateo, lock in the delivery slot.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Furniture schedule. Sven?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: Furniture's booked for the fourteenth, but I got a call that the crew might be, hm, a day late, because of the other site-

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: How late?

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: One day. Maybe two.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Two would hurt, I think? Because of the move-in date.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Which move-in date?

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: The nineteenth. Staff start arriving then. I think.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: It is. I checked it with HR yesterday.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Then we can't slip past the eighteenth. Sven, push them.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: I'll push. Yes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Also, who's got the sample planks?

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: Norvik is sending three boxes.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Good, I can test them.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Test what?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Whatever. Spills, mopping. I like to break stuff.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Fine, but don't delay anything for it.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I won't.

utterances.speaker: Elif
utterances.text: Is anyone doing the, um, budget revisions?

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Me, Friday.

utterances.speaker: Mateo
utterances.text: I can help.

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Thanks. Okay, that's it.

utterances.speaker: Sven
utterances.text: One more thing, there's a, a coffee machine thing-

utterances.speaker: Tariq
utterances.text: Email me.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, um, is everyone here? I think maybe we can start, Ravi's still, oh, no, he just joined.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Badge reader at the front was down again.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Again? That's the third time this month.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Fourth, if you count the garage one.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Okay, so, um, first thing. I heard back from Marisol on the contract. Sort of.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Sort of?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: She said she has the draft from the vendor and she's, she's going through it. She said, I think, end of next week for a first pass.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: End of next week. Is that a real end of next week or a lawyer end of next week?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: I, um, I honestly don't know. I'll ask her to be more specific.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: She told me once two weeks and it was five days. So you never know.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Or it was nine days. Depends who you ask.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Fair, fair.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Did she say anything about the data part? Where the invoices are stored?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: She mentioned there's a section on that. Um, I didn't, I didn't get the details.

utterances.speaker: Ivan
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like to see it when she's done. If that's allowed.

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: Yes, of course. I'll forward it to you. All of you, actually.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: And the second demo? Did the vendor give us any dates?

utterances.speaker: Aisha
utterances.text: They offered two. Um, the Tuesday and the Thursday after next. I think maybe Thursday is better because of the close.

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Thursday's fine with me. As long as it's the afternoon, I have the, the thing with the auditors in the morning.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Which auditors? Tomasz's lot?

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Yeah. The prep call.

utterances.speaker: Ravi
utterances.text: Right. I'm in that one too, I think. Wait, no, that's the one Stefan moved.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
utterances.text: Stefan moved it to Wednesday. I got the invite, then another one, then I'm not sure which-

utterances.speaker: Camila
utterances.text: Pavel, it's the second one. The first one got cancelled.

utterances.speaker: Pavel
